title: Off the shelf vs custom compliance training
seoTitle: Off the shelf vs custom training
description: Off the shelf compliance training is ready made and quick to deploy; custom training is built for your roles, risks, and procedures. When each fits.
shortAnswer: Off the shelf compliance training is ready made content, written for a general audience, that can be licensed and deployed quickly at low cost. Custom compliance training is designed for a specific organization's roles, risks, systems, and procedures. Off the shelf covers the general law and common scenarios well; custom covers how obligations apply in your own workplace. Many regulated organizations use off the shelf content with tailored additions.
keyTakeaways: Off the shelf is faster and cheaper to start; custom costs more but fits the organization's actual work.
Regulators increasingly expect training to fit the nature of the work and risks, which generic content may not fully address.
The biggest gap in off the shelf content is usually local procedure: who to call, which system, what threshold.
Tailoring a generic core with organization specific modules is a common middle path.

sections.heading: What is the core difference between off the shelf and custom compliance training?

blocks.text: The core difference is who the content is written for: off the shelf training is written for many organizations at once, while custom training is written for one. Generic content explains the rule; custom content explains how the rule works in your organization, with your procedures, systems, and examples.

That difference matters because many training obligations are framed around fit to the actual work. In Australia, for example, the Work Health and Safety Regulations 2011 (Cth) require training to be "suitable and adequate" having regard to "the nature of the work carried out by the worker", "the nature of the risks associated with the work", and "the control measures implemented" ([WHS Regulations 2011, r 39](https://www.legislation.gov.au/F2011L02664/latest/text)). Generic content can explain hazards in general; it cannot know your control measures.

Similarly, in vocational training, the Australian Skills Quality Authority (ASQA) expects Registered Training Organisations to contextualize assessment tools to the student cohort and industry or work context, suggests they show how they "tailor off-the-shelf tools", and lists as a known risk "Reliance on purchased assessment tools that are not contextualised to your student cohort" ([ASQA](https://www.asqa.gov.au/for-providers/standards-for-RTOs/practice-guides/quality-area-1-training-and-assessment/assessment-practice-guide)). That rule applies to RTOs, but the principle transfers to workplace programs.

blocks.text: Choose off the shelf when the obligation is general, the risk is similar across organizations, and speed or cost matters most; choose custom when how people comply depends on your own procedures, systems, or risk profile. The higher the consequence of getting it wrong locally, the stronger the case for custom content.

sections.heading: How can off the shelf and custom training be combined?

blocks.text: They can be combined by using off the shelf content for the general legal baseline and custom modules for local application. This keeps cost down while closing the gap that generic content leaves.

items: Map each obligation to the knowledge people need, splitting general law from local procedure ([how to map training to compliance obligations](/guides/how-to-map-training-to-compliance-obligations)).
Check what the off the shelf module actually covers against that map, rather than relying on its title.
Build short custom modules or briefings for the gaps: internal policy, reporting lines, systems, and examples from your own work.
Add role specific assessment so completion of the generic module is not the only evidence.
Review both when the law or your procedures change, and record which version each person completed.

blocks.text: See also [how to design a compliance training program](/guides/how-to-design-a-compliance-training-program) and [e-learning vs instructor led compliance training](/compare/elearning-vs-instructor-led-compliance-training).

sections.heading: What hidden costs should you consider?

blocks.text: The hidden costs are different for each: off the shelf content costs more than its license when it fails to change behavior, and custom content costs more than its build when it is hard to maintain. Both should be judged on total cost over several years, not first year price.

items: **Off the shelf:** time staff spend on content that does not apply to them, supplementary briefings to fill gaps, and limited ability to edit when your procedures change.

**Custom:** ongoing maintenance when the law changes, the need for subject matter expert time, and the risk that content drifts from source policy if it is not structured for updates ([how to update training when regulations change](/guides/how-to-update-training-when-regulations-change)).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry builds custom training from the organization's own policies and obligations, structured so that each concept links to its source. It can also be used to map what an existing off the shelf library covers against the organization's framework, showing where tailored content is needed.

faqs.q: Is off the shelf compliance training enough for an audit?
faqs.a: It can be part of the evidence. Auditors often ask whether training reflects the organization's own risks and procedures. Off the shelf content with a record of tailored additions and role specific assessment is usually more persuasive than generic content alone.

faqs.q: What does tailoring mean in practice?
faqs.a: Adding your own policies, reporting lines, systems, thresholds, and realiztic examples from your work, and removing content that does not apply. It can be done by editing licensed content where permitted or by adding short organization specific modules alongside it.

faqs.q: Who keeps custom training legally current?
faqs.a: The organization, or the partner it engages. Build in a review trigger for legal and procedural change and assign an owner for each module. Structuring content so each point links to its source makes these reviews much faster.

faqs.q: Is custom training always more effective?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Custom content that is poorly designed, text heavy, or out of date can perform worse than good generic content. Relevance helps, but it still needs sound instructional design and assessment.
